82008.subject: Game Over
82008.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/eaa70932-7ce4-467e-b338-a662ed575d6a/0xR_NL_Banner_Heading_Wordmark.jpg?t=1776775276)
Caption: 

Yesterday, Citrini Research published a “[State of the Themes](https://www.citriniresearch.com/p/state-of-the-themes-556)” report, pointing to the conclusion that the playbook that worked since 2023 has stopped working. For crypto, the more interesting question is what sits on the other side of that trade. We think our Bottom Signals framework offers an answer.

Since its May 2023 inception, the Citrindex has returned more than 2.5x the S&P 500 by riding broad baskets in AI, fiscal primacy, GLP-1s, robotics, energy and defense. The shop now argues the conditions behind that monster run are gone. Valuations are no longer cheap, sentiment is no longer bleak, and narratives have drifted toward unprofitable names priced on 2030 TAMs. The core call is that AI capex growth has peaked. Annualized hyperscaler capex is approaching $1T against roughly $200B of ecosystem ARR, and doubling spend from here would require revenue measured in the trillions. 

Large-scale capex commitments are fading, hyperscalers are leaning on debt and equity issuance beyond free cashflows, bottlenecks create real execution risks, and pricing power is eroding, evidenced by OpenAI’s July 30 token price cut that pulled share from Anthropic and revealed real demand elasticity.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/df0b860a-ed26-4d04-a3f6-61c5823e840d/image.png?t=1793889417)
Caption: 

If AI-led Nasdaq leadership is past peak expectations, the natural follow-up for crypto allocators is how stretched that leadership already is against BTC. That relationship is the foundation of our July report, [Bottom Signals](https://app.blockworks.com/report/bottom-signals).

We started from an uncomfortable fact. BTC has been flat against the Nasdaq since November 2017, nearly nine years, while carrying far higher volatility. Adjusted for risk, it has underperformed. As the asset matures, we expect diminishing returns in both directions. Passive, always-long exposure earns progressively less, and outperformance against equity benchmarks increasingly depends on knowing when to be overweight.

Our primary signal leaned on the NAS100/BTC ratio, and the weekly RSI of that pair. Q2 2026 was the most overbought the Nasdaq had been against BTC on record, and on a high timeframe. Said simply, the Nasdaq was blown out to the upside against BTC, driven by the blockbuster rallies in semis, memory, and the AI-bottleneck trade; it was time to take the other side. 

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/2c0ceb83-912d-4a14-8fe2-08af4aa4ee5a/image.jpeg?t=1793889417)

🧠 Crypto News Brief: Crypto shrugged off the midterm shock: Bitcoin reclaimed $80K on a short squeeze and returning ETF inflows, even as a Democratic Congress dims the CLARITY Act's odds and Binance-hack fallout keeps regulators focused on security. 📈 Bitcoin Reclaims $80K as Shorts Get Squeezed Bitcoin climbed back above $80,000 after briefly sliding toward $75,600 as U.S. midterm results came in. Roughly $378 million in bearish bets were liquidated within an hour, while spot BTC ETFs logged $74.6M in net inflows on Nov. 4, snapping a three-day outflow streak worth about $1.16B. Traders now eye resistance near $81,300–$82,000. Read full story 🏦 Fed and OCC Check Bank Defenses After Binance Hack Federal Reserve and OCC supervisors began calling U.S. banks to ask about vulnerabilities, unusual activity or service disruptions following last week's record $6.3 billion Binance heist, Reuters reported citing sources. One major bank's cybersecurity team is drafting an internal review, and sources flagged fast-evolving AI as a key challenge. Both regulators declined to comment. More details 🗳️ Democratic Sweep Puts the CLARITY Act on Life Support Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate, further dimming prospects for the CLARITY Act, the market-structure bill that already failed to advance in September under Republican control. Industry voices told CoinDesk the bill is likely dead in its current form. The new Congress is seated Jan. 3, 2027, while the SEC and CFTC can keep writing rules under existing authority. Read more 🔀 Trump Media Moves $342M in Bitcoin to Crypto.com Wallets attributed to Trump Media & Technology Group sent about 4,259 BTC — roughly $342 million — to Crypto.com, according to Arkham data. On-chain moves do not prove a sale, and the company described earlier transfers as custody or trading management. The amount nearly matches BTC pledged as convertible-note collateral ahead of a Nov. 30 noteholder repayment date. See details 🇭🇰 Hong Kong Passes Crypto Tax Reporting Law Hong Kong adopted the OECD's Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework into law. From 2027, exchanges and other covered providers must collect customer identities, tax residency and records of purchases, sales, crypto-to-crypto swaps and transfers to external wallets, with data shared with overseas tax authorities from 2028.
